name: tls
description: TLS with a private PKI: cleartext vs TLS on the wire, TLS 1.2 vs 1.3 handshakes (what is visible), decryption with a key log, round trips measured through a 50 ms relay (1.3, 1.2, resumption, HelloRetryRequest), ten certificate failures in Go and curl, SNI and the default certificate, protocol-version mismatch, mTLS, and a TLS-inspecting middlebox across curl, Go and Python

checks.name: HTTP Basic auth over plain HTTP: the credentials cross the wire readable

run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -sS -u alice:s3cret http://shop.test/

checks.name: decode it: Basic auth is base64, not encryption
the same over HTTPS: no credentials in the capture — but the name (SNI) is still in cleartext

run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -sS -u alice:s3cret --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test/ >/dev/null && echo fetched

checks.name: a TLS 1.3 and a TLS 1.2 handshake to the same site, captured

run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -s -o /dev/null --http1.1 --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test/ && curl -s -o /dev/null --http1.1 --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test:8443/ && echo both

checks.name: what a passive observer can read: in 1.3 only ClientHello (1) and ServerHello (2); in 1.2 also Certificate (11), ServerKeyExchange (12), ServerHelloDone (14), ClientKeyExchange (16)
run: tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/handshakes.pcap -Y 'tls.handshake' -T fields -E separator=' ' -e ip.src -e tcp.dstport -e tls.handshake.type -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name -e frame.len 2>/dev/null

checks.name: the same request with SSLKEYLOGFILE set: curl writes the session secrets

run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; rm -f ${EVIDENCE}/keys.log; SSLKEYLOGFILE=${EVIDENCE}/keys.log curl -s -o /dev/null --http1.1 --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test/; cut -d' ' -f1 ${EVIDENCE}/keys.log | sort

checks.name: with the key log, Wireshark (tshark) decrypts it: the encrypted handshake (8 EncryptedExtensions, 11 Certificate, 15 CertificateVerify, 20 Finished, 4 NewSessionTicket) and the GET
run: tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/keylog.pcap -o tls.keylog_file:${EVIDENCE}/keys.log -Y 'http.request or tls.handshake.type==11' -T fields -E separator=' ' -e tls.handshake.type -e http.request.method -e http.host -e http.request.uri 2>/dev/null

checks.name: through a relay that adds 50 ms per round trip: a TLS 1.3 handshake costs one round trip, and so does a resumed one
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect 198.18.90.1:4443 -servername shop.test -resume -alpn http/1.1 | grep handshake

checks.name: TLS 1.2: two round trips for a full handshake, one when the session is resumed
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect 198.18.90.1:4444 -servername shop.test -resume -alpn http/1.1 | grep handshake

checks.name: a server that only accepts P-256: the client's X25519/ML-KEM key shares are refused (HelloRetryRequest), costing a second round trip — every time
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect 198.18.90.1:4445 -servername shop.test -resume -alpn http/1.1 | grep handshake

checks.name: curl's view of the same three paths: %{time_appconnect} is when TLS finished
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; for p in 4443 4444 4445; do curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem --connect-to shop.test:443:198.18.90.1:$p -w "port $p: tcp %{time_connect} s, tls done %{time_appconnect} s\n" https://shop.test/; done

checks.name: ClientHello sizes: Go 1.24 offers a post-quantum hybrid key share (X25519MLKEM768), curl/OpenSSL 3.0 does not

run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -s -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test/; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:443 >/dev/null; echo done

checks.name: the two ClientHellos' frame sizes, from the capture
run: tshark -r ${EVIDENCE}/clienthello.pcap -Y 'tls.handshake.type==1' -T fields -e frame.len 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1{print "curl ClientHello frame: "$1" bytes"} NR==2{print "Go ClientHello frame: "$1" bytes"}'

checks.name: the client's system trust store does not know the lab root: a perfectly good chain is 'unknown'
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -connect shop.test:443 | grep -E 'verify|go error'; curl -sS -o /dev/null https://shop.test/ 2>&1 | head -1
expect_contains: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
unable to get local issuer certificate

checks.name: trusting the lab root: the chain shop.test → Lab Issuing CA 1 → Lab Root CA verifies
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:443
expect_contains: OK: shop.test → Lab Issuing CA 1 → Lab Root CA

checks.name: eleven sites, one trust anchor — what Go's crypto/x509 says about each
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; for n in shop.test noint.shop.test expired.shop.test future.shop.test wrong.shop.test a.wild.test wild.test a.b.wild.test self.shop.test rogue.shop.test eku.shop.test; do r=$(${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect $n:443 2>&1 | grep -E 'go error|: OK' | sed 's/.*go error: //; s/.*: OK:.*/OK/'); echo "$n → $r"; done
expect_contains: noint.shop.test → x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
expired.shop.test → x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
wrong.shop.test → x509: certificate is valid for other.test, not wrong.shop.test
wild.test → x509: certificate is valid for *.wild.test, not wild.test
eku.shop.test → x509: certificate specifies an incompatible key usage
self.shop.test → x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

checks.name: the same eleven through curl (OpenSSL): exit 60 and OpenSSL's wording
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; for n in shop.test noint.shop.test expired.shop.test future.shop.test wrong.shop.test a.wild.test wild.test a.b.wild.test self.shop.test rogue.shop.test eku.shop.test; do r=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem https://$n/ 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$n → exit $rc $(echo "$r" | head -1 | sed 's/^curl: //')"; done
expect_contains: noint.shop.test → exit 60 (60) SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'wrong.shop.test'

checks.name: the missing intermediate, close up: the server sent only the leaf
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect noint.shop.test:443 | grep -E 'chain sent|note|meaning'

checks.name: no SNI (connecting by IP): the server falls back to its default certificate, for another name
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect 198.18.91.10:443 | grep -E 'SNI|subject|go error'

checks.name: a server that only speaks TLS 1.0/1.1: modern clients refuse — Go and curl both report a protocol version alert
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:1443 | grep -E 'go error'; curl -sS -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test:1443/ 2>&1 | head -1

checks.name: mTLS without a client certificate: in TLS 1.3 the handshake 'succeeds' and the rejection arrives with the first read
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:9443 | grep -E 'handshake|FAILED|meaning'; curl -sS -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem https://shop.test:9443/ 2>&1 | head -1

checks.name: with a client certificate from the lab CA: accepted, and the server knows who called
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -sS --cacert $P/root.pem --cert $P/client-chain.pem --key $P/client.key https://shop.test:9443/

checks.name: with a client certificate from another CA: curl sends it, the server rejects it (Go would not even send it)
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; curl -sS -o /dev/null --cacert $P/root.pem --cert $P/rogue-client-chain.pem --key $P/rogue-client.key https://shop.test:9443/ 2>&1 | head -1; echo; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:9443 -cert $P/rogue-client-chain.pem -key $P/rogue-client.key | grep -E 'FAILED|meaning'; grep 'unknown authority' ${EVIDENCE}/service-server-mtls.log | tail -1

checks.name: turn on TLS inspection: redirect forwarded port 443 to the intercepting proxy
the client now sees a certificate issued by 'Corp TLS Inspection CA', not the lab's CA
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:443 | grep -E 'issuer|verify|go error'
expect_contains: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

checks.name: from the router itself (not redirected) the real chain is unchanged: comparing issuers inside and outside proves inspection
run: unset SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY http_proxy ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; P=$NETLAB_EVIDENCE/pki; ${BIN}/tlslab inspect -cafile $P/root.pem -connect shop.test:443 | grep -E 'issuer|verify'
expect_contains: OK: shop.test → Lab Issuing CA 1 → Lab Root CA

checks.name: three runtimes, each trusting only the lab root: all fail, each in its own words
expect_contains: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority

checks.name: the fix is trust, configured per runtime: a bundle with the inspection CA added
the proxy's own log: one real connection per intercepted client connection
expect_contains: real certificate issued by "Lab Issuing CA 1", client shown one from "Corp TLS Inspection CA"

checks.name: turn inspection off
